subject: Runtime contracts & parser integration - onboarding plan

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Dana Park <dana.park@novushealth.com>, Novus Health Technical <tech@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Runtime contracts & parser integration - onboarding plan

Hi Dana / Novus team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — excited to get the Runtime + structured output parser into your staging flow. I attached a first-pass runtime contract (PDF) and a small zip with three parser schema examples. High level asks from our side so we can kick off implementation next week: 

- Confirm acceptance criteria for structured outputs (examples in parser_schema_examples.zip).
- Confirm whether Novus will host the post-processing step (parser) behind your VPC or if Redwood should deploy the parser in a private tenant.
- Legal: quick review & sign of the runtime contract (novus_runtime_contract_v1.pdf). We can accept a redline or a DocuSign sign-off.
- Schedule: propose Tech Walkthrough (60 min) on Wed 2027-04-07 10:00 AM PT. Please confirm or suggest an alternate slot.

Technical notes included in the zip: example JSON schemas for streaming sequences, function/tool-calling examples where the model emits a tool call event, and a small section on error semantics (how missing fields are handled). If you want, we can lock the schema to a strict JSON schema or allow an optional freeform field for initial rollout.

Next steps: please reply with which items you want to cover on the walkthrough and any immediate blocking concerns.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: novus_runtime_contract_v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages), parser_schema_examples.zip (3 files)

From: Dana Park <dana.park@novushealth.com>

Cc: Novus Health Technical <tech@novushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Runtime contracts & parser integration - onboarding plan

Irene — thanks for the concise plan and the artifacts. A few clarifying questions before we commit the walkthrough slot:

1) Security boundary for function/tool calls: our security team needs to know whether tool-call payloads will ever touch Redwood-managed storage in plaintext. Can you confirm the call flow if we choose the private-tenant option vs Redwood-hosted parser?

2) Schema versioning: the examples look good but we need an explicit migration path (v1 -> v2). Is there tooling on your side to validate incoming streams and reject malformed messages with a clear error code?

3) SLAs: the runtime contract mentions latency SLOs, but can you confirm whether there is a minimum throughput commitment for burst windows? Our clinicians may run large batches during after-hours.

We can tentatively take the Wed 4/7 10:00 AM PT slot. I'll include our lead engineer (tech@novushealth.com) on the call if that works.

On the contract: legal will review but will likely request two small redlines — one around data retention and one around audit logging frequency.

Thanks,
Dana Park
Director of Product, Novus Health
dana.park@novushealth.com

Dana — quick follow-up after our internal syncs. Thanks for confirming the tentative Wed slot. A few answers and next steps before the walkthrough: 

1) Security boundary: if Novus hosts the parser in your VPC, none of the post-processed payloads will be stored in Redwood-managed storage. The simple call flow is: model -> streaming response (encrypted in transit) -> Novus parser endpoint (over TLS) -> Novus storage. If you choose Redwood-managed private-tenant parser, we encrypt at rest and provide KMS-backed keys; we do not store any plaintext logs beyond a short retention window configured in the contract (default 30 days). I've flagged the retention clause for Lauren to expedite legal language.

2) Schema versioning & validation: Marissa will deliver a JSON Schema test harness. It will run validations on incoming stream fragments and return structured error codes (4xx-like codes for client formatting errors, 5xx for transient runtime issues). We'll include a migration guide for v1->v2 and a compatibility mode where unknown fields are emitted to a reserved "extras" object instead of failing the whole message.

3) SLA and burst commitments: Ben will present throughput sims tomorrow. For burst windows we can commit to a best-effort burst buffer with configurable autoscale and a dedicated burst pool (if you take the reserved capacity add-on). We'll surface the expected queueing behavior and tail latency tradeoffs during the walkthrough.

Attached: novus_runtime_contract_v1.pdf (with callouts), parser_schema_examples.zip. Meeting: Wed Apr 7 10:00 AM PT confirmed — Tech invite sent to tech@novushealth.com.

Please send any contract redlines to lauren.bishop@redwood.com and we'll consolidate. Looking forward to the walkthrough.

Best,
Irene
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
